name: Corvus
introduction: is the Crow. In Greek myth, Apollo sent the crow to fetch water in a cup; the bird lingered, then blamed a water snake. Apollo placed the crow, the cup, Crater, and the snake, Hydra, in the sky, with the crow forever kept from drinking. Its four bright stars form a distinctive quadrilateral, best seen on northern spring evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Corvus is a good example of how Bayer’s Greek letters do not always follow brightness: [Alchiba](hip:59199), Alpha Corvi, is fainter than all four stars of the quadrilateral.
The four stars [Gienah](hip:59803), [Kraz](hip:61359), [Algorab](hip:60965) and [Minkar](hip:59316) form a sail-like shape sometimes called Spica’s Spanker, pointing toward Spica in Virgo.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Gienah](hip:59803) is the brightest star, a blue-white giant about 150 light-years away. [Algorab](hip:60965) is a white star with a faint companion. [Eta Corvi](hip:61174), 60 light-years away, is surrounded by a disk of dust that may come from colliding comets.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The Antennae Galaxies, NGC 4038 and NGC 4039, are two spiral galaxies in the middle of a collision. Their encounter has stretched out long tails of stars resembling an insect’s antennae and triggered bursts of star formation.
